args.query: Patagonia top hiking trails Torres del Paine W trek

answer:
The web search tool returned "No relevant results" for all three queries I tried, so I couldn't pull live search results. Instead, here's what I know from training data about Patagonia's best hikes — no URLs, so treat these as a starting point, not verified links:

Chilean side (Torres del Paine national park)
- W Trek — the classic ~5-day route across the park's "W" shape: base of the Torres, French Valley (Valle Francés), and the Grey Glacier. The single most famous hike in Patagonia.
- O Circuit — a 7–10 day loop that extends the W with the northern pampa and more remote terrain.
- Torres del Paine base hike — a shorter 3–4 hour round trip to the three granite towers; doable as a day trip.
- Fitz Roy / Cerro Torre area (Los Glaciares is Argentine, but the Paine side offers glacier views of Grey and John Gardner).

Argentine side (Los Glaciares national park, El Calafate / El Chaltén)
- Laguna de los Tres — the iconic 10–12 km round trip to the viewpoint below Fitz Roy; the signature El Chaltén hike.
- Cerro Torre viewpoint — a shorter, similarly scenic trail in the same town.
- Perito Moreno glacier walkways — not a "hike" but a must-see; the calving front is spectacular.
- Viedma glacier trek — a guided full-day glacier trek from El Calafate.
- Laguna del Desierto — a remote, multi-day trek in the far south; very wild and low-traffic.

Other notable
- Laguna San Rafael glacier (El Chaltén area) and the Chaltén circuit.
- The Dientes de Navarino circuit on Navarino Island (Ushuaia region) — often called the best short trek in Tierra del Fuego.
- Condor trail and other routes in Chilean Aysén region (e.g., the Quillayín valley / Cerro Diente de Navarino).

Caveats: my knowledge has a cutoff, and trail conditions, entry fees, and permit requirements change frequently — especially post-2024. Before you commit to any of these, check the current park websites (paukenparken / CONAF for Chile; PGN Argentina for the Argentine parks) and recent trip reports for the specific season you're planning.
